data.hypothesis: A factor-three target tile with 128 threads should reuse each streamed source position and mass across three targets while using fewer force accumulators per thread than the factor-four parent. The 384-output block tile changes CTA size and scheduling; register pressure and occupancy effects are uncertain, so this is a measured candidate, not an assumed speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: These results are from the current CUDA N-body campaign; they motivate testing an intermediate factor but do not establish a performance cause.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline measured 0.001847 s. Factor-two candidates measured about 0.002617–0.002727 s and the factor-four candidate measured 0.004442 s; all were correct but slower than baseline. The results do not include register or occupancy measurements.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this factor-three, 128-thread configuration with the full correctness suite and official timing metric.

data.notes: This experiment uses register-level target reuse only; shared-memory staging remains disabled. The factor-three mapping bounds-checks each target, so the final partial tile covers arbitrary N without writing invalid outputs. Correctness and performance remain for the controller to evaluate.
transformations: Map each thread to three output targets separated by blockDim.x and accumulate each target's force independently.
Load each source particle's position and mass once per source-loop iteration and reuse those values across valid targets; do not stage sources in shared memory.
Use 128 threads and 384 outputs per block to match the three-target mapping.
Bounds-check all three target indices, retain self-interaction exclusion, and store every valid output once while preserving the force and integration calculations.
